annotations.title: Welch Allyn PanOptic Plus Ophthalmoscope | Welch Allyn | Hillrom
Welch Allyn Ophthalmic Sets | Welch Allyn | Hillrom

content.text:
Welch Allyn ophthalmology/eye-exam tools are mainly handheld diagnostic instruments used in primary care, optometry, ophthalmology, and training settings. The current Welch Allyn eye-tool lineup is sold under Baxter/Hillrom.

**Common Welch Allyn ophthalmology tools:**

| Tool | What it’s for | Notable Welch Allyn options |
|---|---|---|
| **Direct ophthalmoscope** | Viewing retina, optic disc, vessels, red reflex | **PanOptic Plus**, **3.5 V Coaxial**, **Prestige Coaxial-Plus** |
| **Retinoscope** | Objective refraction; estimating refractive error | **Elite 3.5 V Streak Retinoscope** |
| **Ophthalmic diagnostic sets** | Bundles with ophthalmoscope/retinoscope heads + rechargeable handle | Welch Allyn 3.5 V ophthalmic sets |
| **iExaminer system** | Digital image capture with compatible PanOptic ophthalmoscope | iExaminer Pro add-on system |
| **Power handles/chargers** | Rechargeable power source for 3.5 V instrument heads | 3.5 V rechargeable and Lithium Ion Plus handles |

The **PanOptic Plus Ophthalmoscope** is Welch Allyn’s newer wide-view direct ophthalmoscope. Baxter/Hillrom lists it as having a **20× larger viewing area** than a standard or pocket ophthalmoscope, LED illumination, Quick Eye alignment lights, and compatibility with Welch Allyn 3.5 V handles and wall transformers. ([hillrom.com](https://www.hillrom.com/en/products/panoptic-plus-ophthalmoscope/?utm_source=openai))

The **Welch Allyn Ophthalmic Sets** typically include a rechargeable 3.5 V handle and an ophthalmoscope head; current sets emphasize LED illumination and may include the PanOptic Plus. ([hillrom.com](https://www.hillrom.com/en/products/ophthalmic-sets/?utm_source=openai))

For refraction, the **Welch Allyn Elite Retinoscope** is a 3.5 V streak retinoscope. Baxter/Hillrom lists features such as a crossed-linear polarizing filter to reduce glare, an external focusing sleeve, sealed optics, and compatibility with 3.5 V power sources. ([hillrom.com](https://www.hillrom.com/en/products/elite-retinoscope/?utm_source=openai))

**Which one to choose:**

- **Medical/PA/nursing student:** a basic Welch Allyn ophthalmoscope/otoscope set is usually enough unless your school requires a specific model.
- **Primary care clinic:** PanOptic Plus is easier for many non-eye specialists because of its wider view.
- **Optometry/ophthalmology training:** consider the **Elite Retinoscope** plus a standard or PanOptic ophthalmoscope.
- **Need image capture/documentation:** look at **PanOptic Plus + iExaminer Pro**.
- **Buying used:** check that the head works, optics are clean, lenses rotate smoothly, the handle holds charge, and bulbs/LEDs are available.

If you’re asking because you want to **buy** one, tell me your use case—student, clinic, home use, optometry, ophthalmology, or veterinary—and your budget, and I can narrow down the best Welch Allyn set.
